axes.model_access: Its own generation line: the same-day site headline wording is "trained only on music we create in-house" (the 100% Copyright-Safe narrative) — training data self-described as an in-house catalog; no third-party model picking.
axes.runtime: Web product (soundraw.io); generation runs on SOUNDRAW's cloud; the Mixer surface (toggle instrument tracks / adjust intensity / set length) on record same day; no API/local surface verified in official statements.
axes.local_files: Downloaded exported audio is yours locally; generation and the catalog live on SOUNDRAW's side; no locally-held data surface declared by the vendor was found.
axes.background: Generation returns instantly per the narrative ("in seconds"); queueing/resume details not verified item by item.
axes.tools: Editing surface on record (per-track Mixer toggles/intensity/length, Blend Genres style mixing); no MCP/API support verified in official statements.
axes.context: Works are organized in the account's track library and can be revisited and re-edited; no official statement verified for cross-session memory (say unknown when unknown).
axes.permissions: Account system (free + subscription); "royalty-free" is the lead narrative — every beat is "legally yours to use, monetize, and share" on record on the site same day; exact tier licensing boundaries follow the ToS, not verified item by item.
axes.fit: Fits: royalty-free scoring for video/podcasts, fast pick-and-edit by mood/genre/length, a "self-claimed clean training data" copyright narrative. Not a fit: a filed direct-mainland entry, vocal songs with lyrics (instrumental beats are the pitch), running models locally.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to audio products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Third-party verification of the "in-house training" narrative** (the self-claim is on record; audits/catalog provenance are not — this is its core differentiator and deserves standalone due diligence)
- **Actual granularity of the per-track Mixer** (instrument-track toggles/intensity/length effects not verified in engineering terms)
- **Whether rights to already-downloaded tracks survive subscription cancellation** (ToS not verified item by item)
unknowns:
- Size and provenance of the in-house catalog (the site narrative gives no numbers)
- Exact tier prices and licensing differences (the pricing page is JS-rendered; not fetched item by item)
- Whether an API surface exists (no official statement verified)
- Whether exported tracks keep their license after a subscription lapses (ToS not verified item by item)
related: Also full-song generation but the opposite route: Suno leads with vocal pop, SOUNDRAW's instrumental beats lead with royalty-free scoring.
